Theses

High school agricultural students' perceptions of agripreneurship and the future of agriculture in the Ashanti Region of Ghana

MSc Agricultural Economics, Akdeniz University, Türkiye · 2024–2026 · Supervisor: Assoc. Prof. Dr. Yavuz Taşcıoğlu

Ghana needs young people to replace an ageing farming population, yet few agricultural science graduates move into agribusiness. This study asked whether students who see a positive future for agriculture are more likely to plan an agricultural enterprise, and what holds them back. It used a convergent mixed-methods design: a stratified survey of 274 students in eight public senior high schools across eight districts, with four 5-point Likert scales (Cronbach's α = 0.937–0.984; KMO = 0.964–0.977) and seven open-ended questions.

274students surveyed in 8 schools
70.0%of variance in intention explained by perception (β = 0.833)
13.84odds ratio for high intention linked to positive perception
26.2%named poor tools and facilities as the main barrier
  • Perception of agriculture (OR = 13.84) and entrepreneurial traits (OR = 11.22) both predicted high intention in Firth-corrected logistic regression; gender, residence and parents' education did not.
  • Students named economic incentives (23.4%) and government support (14.6%) as their main motivators, and limited practical experience (16.2%) and outdated curriculum content (15.1%) as further barriers.
  • Analysed in SPSS and R (correlation, t-tests, ANOVA, chi-square, multiple linear regression), with thematic and SWOT coding of the open-ended answers.

Financial viability of aquaponics systems in the Ashanti Region

BSc Agribusiness Management, KNUST, Ghana · 2021 · Group dissertation (five students) · Supervisor: Dr. Gifty Boakye Appiah

Aquaponics produces fish and vegetables from the same water, which suits peri-urban farmers with little land. Five-year cash flows for catfish and tilapia systems were built in Excel from interviews with 12 aquaponics farmers reached by snowball sampling, and production constraints were ranked with Kendall's coefficient of concordance.

GH₵ 60,931NPV for tilapia at a 30% discount rate (catfish GH₵ 49,958)
77%IRR for tilapia (catfish 64%)
1.54benefit–cost ratio for tilapia (catfish 1.45)
W = 0.54agreement on constraints; feed cost ranked first

Both systems were viable, and tilapia paid back faster (5.40 against 6.58 months). High feed cost and power fluctuation were the two most pressing constraints (p < 0.01), which points to feed and energy costs as the first targets for support.

Conference paper

A moderated-mediation analysis of agripreneurial intentions: Assessing agricultural education quality and career perceptions in the Ashanti Region, Ghana

Presented at MEETCON-ANATOLIA, 3rd International Congress of Social and Human Sciences, Gaziantep, Türkiye, 21–25 May 2026

Abstract

Agriculture remains central to Ghana's economy, yet many agricultural science students do not go on to agribusiness careers. This study tested whether career perceptions mediate the link between the quality of agricultural education and students' agripreneurial intentions, and whether that link differs between student groups. Survey data from 274 senior high school agriculture students in eight schools in the Ashanti Region were analysed with PROCESS Models 4 and 7 and 5,000 bootstrap samples.

Education quality had a total effect of β = 0.681 on agripreneurial intentions and explained 51.1% of their variance. It was strongly related to career perceptions (0.622), which were in turn strongly related to intentions (0.751); the indirect effect (β = 0.467) carried about 68.5% of the total. The indirect effect was larger for rural students (0.511) than urban students (0.421), while gender and class level showed no significant difference. The results suggest that agricultural education raises agripreneurial intention mainly by changing how students see farming as a career, and that rural schools may gain most from better facilities and career exposure.

Adufah, S. N., & Taşcıoğlu, Y. (2026). In MEETCON-ANATOLIA: 3rd International Congress of Social and Human Sciences, Book of Proceedings (pp. 212–228). Liberty Publishing House. ISBN 979-8-89695-421-7.

Policy brief

Strengthening agricultural education to increase youth agripreneurship in Ghana

Policy brief, 2026 · Written for the Ministry of Education, Ghana Education Service and the Ministry of Food and Agriculture

The brief turns the conference findings into advice for policymakers. Its central point is that better teaching alone is not enough; schools also need to change how students see agricultural careers, because about two-thirds of education's effect on intention runs through those perceptions.

  1. Add agribusiness management, entrepreneurship, digital agriculture and financial literacy to senior high school agriculture curricula.
  2. Make career exposure an explicit goal: young agripreneur role models, school–industry partnerships, farm visits and mentorship.
  3. Put rural schools first for school farms, practical facilities and laboratories, since rural students showed the stronger indirect effect.

Mapping projects

Independent QGIS projects completed in 2026. Each one starts from a targeting question that an extension service, NGO or programme officer would ask.

Market access and smallholder vulnerability

Ashanti Region, Ghana

Support for smallholders is usually targeted by district, yet travel time to a market varies a great deal within one district. Road speeds were used to model the two-hour travel reach of each market hub with network analysis, drawn as convex hulls. Communities outside every hull sit beyond a workable market network, a gap that district tables do not show.

Map available on request.
Network analysisTravel-time catchmentsConvex hulls

Aquaponics site suitability

Ashanti Region, Ghana · follows on from the BSc study

Rivers and water bodies were buffered and overlaid with markets and settlements to find land within reach of both water and buyers. Suitable zones follow the river network and are densest around Kumasi, which gives programmes a first shortlist of corridors for feed subsidies or starter kits.

Vector buffersAttribute joinsMulti-criteria overlay

Climate stress zones for maize

Ashanti Region, Ghana

March temperature and rainfall rasters were combined and reclassified to flag land at or above 34 °C with 90 mm of rain or less. These high-stress niches fall mainly in the north-eastern districts, which makes them first candidates for heat- and drought-tolerant maize varieties.

Raster CalculatorReclassificationClimate rasters

Maize yield gaps between districts

Northern Region, Ghana

District maize yields were joined to boundaries and mapped in five classes. Yields ranged from 1.2 to 3.63 t/ha, about a threefold gap. Karaga, Saboba and both Nanumba districts sat in the lowest class and Kpandai in the highest, a starting point for directing extension staff and rural credit.

Table joinsChoropleth mapping

Drought stress from Sentinel-2 imagery

Western Brandenburg, Germany · July 2022

NDVI was calculated from Sentinel-2 bands for the agricultural plain during the 2022 summer drought, masked, and grouped into five classes from bare soil to dense vegetation. High stress is concentrated in the north-west of the scene, which shows how satellite data can point field teams to stressed land before a site visit.
